3df39de8d2.q: What are the main differences between asset purchase and stock purchase in a business acquisition?
3df39de8d2.a: Asset purchases offer tax benefits, liability protection, and the option to select which assets to acquire, with accelerated depreciation possibilities. Stock purchases mean taking on existing debt, inheriting all contracts and liabilities, and exposing yourself to hidden risks and unresolved obligations from the seller.
3df39de8d2.e: Key Considerations for Acquiring A Business

0966af51c8.q: What critical due diligence steps must be completed before signing a Letter of Intent in a business acquisition?
0966af51c8.a: You must review P&Ls and tax returns, analyze accounts receivable, understand employee compensation and contracts, review customer contracts and data privacy, verify licenses and certifications, check OSHA compliance, and identify all lease agreements with amendments before signing an LOI. You cannot begin due diligence after signing—it must be done ahead of time.
0966af51c8.e: Key Considerations for Acquiring A Business

77b6dc1b67.q: Why are lease agreements often deal-killers in business acquisitions?
77b6dc1b67.a: Landlords have killed more deals than can be named. You must know every lease, every amendment whether there is one or twenty, renewal options, and whether the lease will cash flow. Increasingly, landlords now negotiate to receive a piece of the sale price as part of the transaction, which must be factored into the deal structure.
77b6dc1b67.e: Key Considerations for Acquiring A Business

70cb197e79.q: What are the main regulatory compliance risks to assess when acquiring a business?
70cb197e79.a: You must verify licensing, data privacy protections, workplace safety (OSHA), EEOC compliance, HIPAA for healthcare, and industry-specific regulations like those for construction or electrical businesses. One misstep on compliance can result in inherited liabilities, fines, and operational shutdowns post-acquisition.
70cb197e79.e: Key Considerations for Acquiring A Business

c6bfdc5f40.q: What percentage of customer base may leave after combining two businesses operationally?
c6bfdc5f40.a: Statistically, 10% to 25% of the customer base may leave when two businesses are combined, particularly when merging banking systems or operational platforms. This attrition must be built into financial projections and transition planning.
c6bfdc5f40.e: Key Considerations for Acquiring A Business

caded5454b.q: Why is selecting the right tax advisor critical in a business acquisition deal?
caded5454b.a: Not all CPAs are created equal; some can calculate tax depreciation, goodwill allocations, sales tax, and non-compete allocations, while others simply prepare tax returns. The buyer and seller must file matching information with the IRS post-acquisition, and mismatches trigger audits. The wrong advisor makes the deal extremely difficult or a deal-killer.
caded5454b.e: Key Considerations for Acquiring A Business

6221c88c08.q: What are the top 10 most common mistakes employers make when terminating employees?
6221c88c08.a: The top 10 preventable mistakes include: failing to document every problem, ignoring your own handbook policies, treating employees differently, terminating after a protected activity such as requesting leave or reporting harassment, holding unemotional and professional termination meetings, failing to investigate complaints before terminating, withholding wages without proper justification, failing to recover company property, not providing separation notice in writing, and failing to consult with legal counsel before termination.

42f25ad1ea.q: What must an employee manual include to provide legal defense in termination disputes?
42f25ad1ea.a: An employee manual should comprehensively cover Title VII discrimination protections, ADA accommodations procedures, Family Medical Leave Act requirements, OSHA safety protocols, Fair Labor Standards Act wage and hour rules, attendance policies, PTO policies, anti-harassment policies both sexual and non-sexual, NDA requirements, social media and internet policies, technology and AI utilization guidelines, progressive discipline procedures, and a clear complaint process. The manual should be 80 to 100 pages covering all these essentials, as it serves as your strongest legal defense in any employment litigation.

38e2fabebe.q: What must be included in a separation letter when an employee is terminated?
38e2fabebe.a: A separation letter must specify the final day of employment, final compensation amount, status of all benefits including PTO accrual, COBRA eligibility, 401k information, detailed requirements for equipment return including keys, computers, tablets, and phones with specific timeframes of 24 to 48 hours, clarification that the employee cannot access company systems or facilities after termination, confidentiality and non-disclosure obligations, and any restrictive covenants or non-compete agreements applicable by state law.

54a1865cf1.q: What are the federal laws employers must consider before terminating an employee?
54a1865cf1.a: Employers must consider Title VII which prohibits discrimination based on race, color, creed, sex, origin, or pregnancy; the America with Disabilities Act which requires reasonable accommodation requests be handled interactively with three possible outcomes: grant, modify, or deny; the Family Medical Leave Act for employers with 50 or more employees; the Age Discrimination in Employment Act which provides protected class status for employees over 40 with different release and severance requirements; and OSHA which protects employees reporting safety violations and prohibits retaliation for such reports.

52ea3e9818.q: What types of retaliation are prohibited when employees report complaints or safety issues?
52ea3e9818.a: Employers absolutely cannot retaliate against employees for reporting harassment claims, filing workers compensation claims, requesting medical leave, complaining about wages, or reporting OSHA safety violations. Retaliation for wrongful termination claims is described as probably one of the biggest and fastest areas for litigation. If federal agencies like OSHA audit your business regarding a termination following an employee complaint, it creates significant legal exposure. Every business should have a process for reporting harassment and anti-retaliation policies in their employee handbooks.

da487a93c3.q: What specific documentation and procedures must employers follow for reasonable accommodation requests under the ADA?
da487a93c3.a: When an employee requests a medical accommodation, employers must have a written accommodation procedure in place. The request should document the medical reasons for the accommodation in writing, and the employer must engage in an interactive process with only three possible outcomes: grant the accommodation, modify it, or deny it with specific justification. Employers cannot discriminate based on disability, and failure to consider reasonable accommodation requests in compliance with federal guidelines creates significant liability with federal authorities.
